classificationReport.severityCriteria: C4 (High = direct/valid-path asset loss w/o hypotheticals; Medium = function/availability impact OR value leak w/ stated assumptions + external reqs; QA/Low = state/spec/centralization). Three-Law hierarchy applied: security > story-faithfulness > owner-trust(knowing-only).
classificationReport.labelScheme: M-01..M-05 (High/Medium, individual + PoC), F-01..F-02 (spec-conformance/faithfulness report), L-01..L-03 (QA bundle). No High this run; no pure-centralization C-labels.
notes: Zero High. This is the honest result: every new value/availability defect is gated on either an external market precondition (underwater strategy) or a non-obvious owner-operational footgun, none of which is an unconditional external-attacker theft path. Overstating any to High would dilute the report (pipeline rejects overstatement).
DEDUP-003 re-weighed Low->Medium (adjudication below). Ledger holds Low(open) and is human-authoritative until /ledger triage; this is a PROPOSED re-weigh surfaced per Law 1, not an auto-overwrite.
DEDUP-005 keyed on emergencyWithdraw and explicitly NOT inheriting buffer-scoped wont-fix 69c7666 (different, strictly-larger bufferless exposure). Surfaced for human wont-fix-coverage re-triage.
DEDUP-002/003/004/006/008 are Law-3 NON-OBVIOUS owner footguns (in scope as operational hazards, classified by unlocked impact), not malicious-admin vectors.

classifiedFindings.label: M-01
classifiedFindings.title: Idle-pool strategy adoption discards strategy.deposit creditedPrincipal — last-withdrawer FCFS shortfall

classification.assetImpact: Last withdrawers on the healthy-withdraw path are shorted principal: setYieldStrategy's adoption sweep (L215) discards strategy.deposit's returned creditedPrincipal, so poolInfo.totalStaked stays at full nominal while strategy.principalOf == idleBalance*(1-slip). The gap is a silent FCFS shortfall and becomes skimmable protocol surplus unrecoverable by users.
attackPath: 1. Pool is populated and held idle (totalStaked = N, idle balance = N).
2. Owner adopts a haircutting/market strategy via setYieldStrategy; sweep books strategy.principalOf = N*(1-slip) but discards the return so totalStaked stays N.
3. Underwater guard is blind (compares strategy totalBalanceOf vs principalOf, both already haircut).
4. Users withdraw FCFS at nominal until the strategy principal is exhausted; the last withdrawer(s) cannot be paid full principal.
classification.likelihood: medium - no attacker needed, but requires the owner to adopt a haircutting strategy over an already-populated idle pool (non-obvious footgun).
classification.assumptions: A market/haircutting IYieldStrategy is adopted onto a non-empty pool (slip > 0).
classification.externalRequirements: Owner adopts the strategy; strategy haircuts deposits.

classifiedFindings.justification: Re-confirmation of already-submitted ledger Medium dab5a656 (PoC passing at HEAD). Value leak with stated assumptions and an external (owner-config) requirement, no direct attacker theft — textbook Medium. The triggering owner action is a non-obvious footgun (a competent owner would not expect 'wiring yield' to permanently desync recoverable principal). Severity unchanged at Medium; emit carryover stub, do not re-report.

classifiedFindings.label: M-02
classifiedFindings.title: setYieldStrategy lacks !active guard — sweeps the realized payout pile R into a strategy, bricks the userMigrate escape hatch and strands migrants' principal
classifiedFindings.knownIssueDistinction: NOT covered by known issue #7 (re-wiring a HEALTHY pool strands funds in the OLD strategy). Here the token is ALREADY in terminal migration: the idle balance IS the realized payout pile R, and there is no in-contract route to recover it (withdraw/emergencyWithdraw blocked while active; initiateMigration is one-shot and already ran; batchMigrate/userMigrate pay from idle balance which is now gone).

classification.assetImpact: After initiateMigration decouples the strategy and parks R as idle balance, calling setYieldStrategy on the migrating token re-approves a strategy and sweeps R back into it (L213-216). batchMigrate/userMigrate then safeTransfer from the (now-empty) idle pile and revert, so EVERY migrant's principal is permanently stranded inside the new strategy with no in-contract recovery path (rescueERC20 only sweeps contract balance, not strategy-held funds; clearing the strategy does not auto-migrate funds back).
attackPath: 1. Owner/migrator engages terminal migration: initiateMigration realizes R into idle balance, clears yieldStrategy[token].
2. Operator (unaware of the interaction) calls setYieldStrategy(token, strat) on the migrating token — no !active guard blocks it.
3. The adoption sweep deposits R into strat; contract idle balance -> ~0.
4. userMigrate/batchMigrate compute credit but safeTransfer reverts (insufficient balance); the permissionless escape hatch is bricked and principal is stranded.
classification.likelihood: low-to-medium - requires a token currently in terminal migration (a dormant 'break-glass' path) AND the owner wiring a strategy onto that exact token mid-migration; compounded operational preconditions, no external attacker.
classification.assumptions: Terminal migration is active for the token; some migrants have not yet exited; owner calls setYieldStrategy on the migrating token.
classification.externalRequirements: Owner action during an active terminal migration.

classifiedFindings.justification: Classified Medium as a Law-3 NON-OBVIOUS owner footgun (a competent owner would be surprised that 'wiring a yield strategy' destroys the migration payout pile). The unlocked impact is severe — escape-hatch availability destroyed plus permanent principal stranding — which is exactly the function/availability-impact band of Medium, and the principal-loss ceiling argues against any downgrade to Low. NOT raised to High: the path is purely owner-operational (no external attacker) and stacks two preconditions (a rare dormant migration plus a mistaken config call during it), so it lacks the unconditional, attacker-executable route High requires. A judge who deems config-during-migration a realistic sequence could argue High; conservatively Medium. Fix: add require(!migrationInfo[token].active) to setYieldStrategy.

classifiedFindings.label: M-03
classifiedFindings.title: Terminal-migration escape hatch is not mint-free: _exitPosition mints frozen pending phUSD before the principal transfer, so a revoked minter mid-migration traps principal

classification.assetImpact: During an active terminal migration the only exits are userMigrate/batchMigrate, both of which mint frozen pending phUSD (L479-481) BEFORE transferring principal. If the old staker's phUSD minter right is revoked while the token is active, every exit with pending > 0 reverts on the mint and the migrant's principal is unrecoverable from the contract until minter rights are restored. Recoverable (not permanently lost), but unavailable.
attackPath: 1. Terminal migration is active; some stakers still hold positions with pending > 0.
2. Operator decommissions the old staker by revoking its phUSD minter right (the natural, non-obvious-consequence step in a migrate-then-retire flow).
3. Remaining users call userMigrate (the permissionless escape hatch); _exitPosition's phUSD.mint reverts; principal is trapped.
4. Funds remain frozen until the owner re-grants minter rights.
classification.likelihood: medium - revoking the old staker's minter during/after migration is a plausible decommissioning sequence; the consequence (trapping in-flight migrants) is non-obvious.
classification.assumptions: Affected users have non-zero pending phUSD (true for active stakers); minter right is revoked while the token is active.
classification.externalRequirements: phUSD minter right revoked from the staker mid-migration (owner action).

classifiedFindings.justification: ADJUDICATION (Low vs Medium): re-weighed to MEDIUM. (a) Availability of the protocol's permissionless escape hatch — the one mechanism that must always let users exit — is impaired under a plausible, non-obvious operational precondition (decommissioning the old staker by revoking its minter), which is the textbook Medium 'function/availability impacted with stated assumptions + external requirements'. (b) It is a Law-2 faithfulness gap: emergencyWithdraw's stated invariant 'a broken mint path can never trap principal' is NOT preserved by its terminal-mode replacement (userMigrate mints before transferring). Held at Medium, NOT High: principal is recoverable once minter rights are restored (temporary unavailability, no permanent loss), which is squarely the 'availability impacted, not direct asset loss' band. A judge could retain Low citing recoverability + owner-precondition; both sides documented. faithfulness:true -> also cross-referenced to the spec-conformance report. Ledger Low(open) remains authoritative until /ledger triage; if accepted as Medium it warrants an individual submission (not QA bundling) and a PoC. Fix: provide a mint-free / pending-deferred terminal exit.

classifiedFindings.label: M-04
classifiedFindings.title: Underwater buffer-path withdraw desyncs totalStaked < strategy.principalOf, making initiateMigration's L392 post-check unsatisfiable — terminal migration permanently un-initiable

relatedLedger.relation: shared SYMPTOM (migration bricked) but DISTINCT upstream cause + code location (new initiateMigration L392 post-check). KEEP DISTINCT - merging would bury a live liveness defect under a likely-fixed/removed-code entry (Law 1: recall > tidiness).

classification.assetImpact: No principal loss; permanent loss of the terminal-migration FEATURE for the affected token. A story-002 underwater buffer-path withdraw (L679-687) decrements pool.totalStaked (L271) without touching strategy principal, leaving strategy.principalOf > totalStaked. initiateMigration requests _routeExit(token, P=totalStaked) which under-drains the strategy, so the L392-395 require(principalOf == 0) reverts on every attempt — the token can never enter terminal migration.
attackPath: 1. A strategy-backed token has an on-contract buffer (per the buffer-at-par design) and the strategy dips underwater.
2. A user withdraws an amount the buffer can cover; _routeExit pays from buffer, totalStaked decremented, strategy principal untouched -> principalOf > totalStaked.
3. Owner/migrator later calls initiateMigration: P = totalStaked under-requests the strategy exit; principalOf remains > 0.
4. The L392 'incomplete exit' require reverts; terminal migration is permanently un-initiable for the token.
classification.likelihood: medium - arises from a normal user withdraw during a transient underwater dip when a buffer exists; no special privilege or attacker.
classification.assumptions: A non-zero on-contract buffer exists for the token (consistent with the documented buffer-at-par design) and at least one buffer-path withdraw occurs while underwater.
classification.externalRequirements: Strategy below par (external market condition) plus an existing buffer.

classifiedFindings.justification: Medium: protocol function/availability is impacted — the terminal-migration / upgrade escape mechanism is permanently bricked for the affected token — with a stated assumption (buffer present) and an external requirement (underwater strategy). No direct asset loss (users retain withdraw/emergencyWithdraw while not migrating), so it does not reach High. Distinct NEW defect from acknowledged/likely-fixed 3d61c955 (different function, different root cause, on code that postdates it); kept distinct to avoid burying a live liveness defect. PoC required.

classifiedFindings.label: M-05
classifiedFindings.title: emergencyWithdraw realizes underwater loss FCFS via direct share over-redemption (bufferless par bank-run): early exiters whole, late exiters absorb the entire shortfall

wontFixCoverageReTriage.verdict: DOES NOT COVER - do not inherit
wontFixCoverageReTriage.detail: MUST key on emergencyWithdraw, NOT _routeExit ('src/StableStaker.sol:_routeExit:fcfs-loss-socialization' hashes to the wont-fix 69c7666). The wont-fix rested on 'no incremental victim vs a no-buffer world' and is bounded by buffer size; this finding is the strictly-larger BUFFERLESS exposure (bounded by the full pool shortfall) where early callers over-redeem shares at the depressed price and there IS an incremental victim relative to pro-rata. Known issue #6 blesses only a SELF-INFLICTED haircut, not inter-user order-externalization. Surfaced for explicit human re-triage.

classification.assetImpact: Inter-user value socialization: emergencyWithdraw passes guardUnderwater=false, so _routeExit redeems requested principal from the strategy at the depressed price. First callers receive full principal (over-redeeming shares), draining the position; late callers receive less than principal or revert, absorbing the entire pre-existing strategy shortfall. Late stakers lose principal to early stakers.
attackPath: 1. The strategy goes underwater (share price < par).
2. A user calls the permissionless emergencyWithdraw; _routeExit -> strategy.withdraw delivers the full requested principal by burning convertToShares(amount) shares at the depressed price.
3. Repeated first-movers exit at ~par, consuming the shared underwater position.
4. The last exiters find insufficient backing and absorb the full shortfall (partial/failed payout).
classification.likelihood: medium - any user can race once the strategy is underwater; gated on the external market precondition that the strategy is below par.
classification.assumptions: Exit ordering determines outcome; the strategy delivers requested assets by over-burning shares when underwater (ERC4626 withdraw(assets) semantics).
classification.externalRequirements: Strategy below par (external market / negative-yield condition).

classifiedFindings.justification: Medium: value leak (inter-user loss socialization) with a stated assumption (exit ordering) and an external requirement (strategy underwater). Not High: the total payout never exceeds the strategy's realizable value — no value is stolen from the protocol; an already-incurred strategy loss is mis-DISTRIBUTED FCFS rather than pro-rata, and the trigger is an external market condition the design treats as transient. Strictly larger than buffer-scoped wont-fix 69c7666 and not blessed by known issue #6; do NOT inherit the wont-fix — surfaced for human re-triage. PoC required (demonstrate two equal-principal users diverging by exit order).

classifiedFindings.label: F-01
classifiedFindings.title: Migration credit asymmetry: operator batchMigrate books users below principal through a haircutting destination strategy while userMigrate keeps full value

classification.assetImpact: Batch-migrated users are booked below their old-staker principal: the migrator redeposits each credit via newStaker.depositFor -> _routeDeposit, which a haircutting destination strategy reduces to credited = amount*(1-slip). A user who instead self-exits via userMigrate receives tokens to their own wallet at full credit. Magnitude = destination slippageToleranceBps; zero when the destination has no/full-credit strategy at migration time.
attackPath: 1. Destination (new) staker has a haircutting strategy wired for the token at migration time.
2. Operator batchMigrate -> migrator -> depositFor -> _routeDeposit haircuts the booked principal for passive (operator-migrated) users.
3. A user who self-migrated via userMigrate avoided the re-deposit and kept full value.
4. Equal-principal users diverge purely by exit method, breaking the migrator's stated principal-preservation / equivalence story.
classification.likelihood: low - requires a haircutting strategy configured on the destination at migration time (freshly deployed targets are typically idle).
classification.assumptions: Destination strategy haircuts deposits (slip > 0) at migration time.

classifiedFindings.justification: Primarily a Law-2 FAITHFULNESS gap: the migrator's documented promise ('preserves principal' / batch and self exits are equivalent) is broken on the deposit side for one of two intended-equivalent exits. Routed to the spec-conformance report (F-01), faithfulness:true. Honest severity LOW, not Medium: the value delta equals the normal entry slippage of a haircutting strategy (the same haircut any new depositor takes), is bounded by slippageToleranceBps, and is config-dependent. Also a non-obvious owner footgun (migrate while the destination has a haircutting strategy). No PoC required at Low; included in spec-conformance with safe-config guidance (migrate into an idle/full-credit destination, or normalize credit across both exit paths).

classifiedFindings.label: F-02
classifiedFindings.title: withdrawDisabled view over-reports: returns raw _isUnderwater after story-002 added the buffer path, so it reads true where a buffer-covered withdraw would succeed

classification.assetImpact: None. UX/spec false-negative only: the public view's documented contract ('true while withdraw is blocked') no longer holds after story-002 made blocking a strict subset of underwater. withdrawDisabled returns _isUnderwater, so it reports true even when an on-contract buffer would let the withdraw succeed.
attackPath: 1. Strategy is underwater but the buffer can cover a given withdraw.
2. withdrawDisabled returns true (over-reports disabled) though withdraw would in fact succeed via the buffer.
3. Off-chain UI may discourage a withdraw that would have worked.
classification.likelihood: n/a - no value at risk; conservative direction only (never under-reports).
classification.assumptions: Off-chain consumers trust the view's stated contract.

classifiedFindings.justification: QA/Low spec deviation, tagged faithfulness:true and routed to the spec-conformance report (F-02) rather than buried in gas noise (Law 2). Not the invalid 'unused view' category — it is a documented public view whose stated behaviour no longer matches the code after story-002. No on-chain dependency, no value at risk, conservative direction only. No PoC required.

classifiedFindings.label: L-01
classifiedFindings.title: phUSDPerDay sub-86400-wei/day budget floors phusdPerSecond to 0 (silent zero emission)
classifiedFindings.scope: Only the sub-86400 SILENT-ZERO edge is classified here; the integer-division DUST component is suppressed under known issue #2 / wont-fix 35e9be8d (see sanitized-findings.suppressed).

classification.assetImpact: None directly. Owner sets amountPerDay < SECONDS_PER_DAY (86400 base units) -> perSecond = amountPerDay/86400 = 0 -> the pool silently emits ZERO rewards with no revert; stakers accrue nothing while believing a budget is live.
attackPath: 1. Owner calls phUSDPerDay(token, amountPerDay) with amountPerDay < 86400.
2. Integer division floors perSecond to 0; the event still emits a (0) rate.
3. Pool accrues zero phUSD indefinitely with no error surfaced.
classification.likelihood: low - requires the owner to set a sub-86400-base-unit daily budget; economically negligible for an 18-decimal phUSD but a genuine silent-failure edge.
classification.assumptions: Owner sets a small-but-positive daily budget below the per-second floor.

classifiedFindings.justification: QA/Low non-obvious owner-config footgun (a competent owner would be surprised a positive daily budget emits zero with no revert). Distinct from the accepted dust class (known issue #2 rounds DOWN, it does not bless a complete zero-emission state). No value at risk for realistic 18-decimal budgets. Recommend a require(perSecond > 0) or input-scaling guard. QA bundle; no PoC required.

classifiedFindings.label: L-02
classifiedFindings.title: Unbounded per-user external-call loop in batchMigrate + StableStakerMigrator.migrate (gas-bound DoS; relocated from removed migrateOut)

ledgerMatch.ledgerAction: RELOCATE entry to batchMigrate L440-445 + Migrator.migrate L76-81 (do NOT mint a duplicate; retain 59eebbf8 as stable id with relocation note).

classification.assetImpact: None. Gas-bound liveness only: a large users[] array in batchMigrate (L440-445) / Migrator.migrate (L76-81) can exceed the block gas limit. No per-user transfer-to-user, so no single-user brick.
attackPath: 1. Operator passes an oversized users[] batch.
2. The loop's cumulative gas exceeds the block limit and reverts.
3. Mitigation already provided: off-chain operator pages batches via getStakersRange.
classification.likelihood: low - operator-controlled batch sizing with pagination helpers already in place; Law-3 operator-trusted.
classification.assumptions: Operator builds batches; getStakers/getStakersRange used for paging.

classifiedFindings.justification: QA/Low gas-bound DoS, re-confirmation of OPEN ledger Low 59eebbf8, semantically relocated from the removed migrateOut to batchMigrate + Migrator.migrate. Operator-controlled and paginable; no value at risk and no per-user brick. Carryover stub; ledger entry should be RELOCATED, not duplicated. No PoC required.

classifiedFindings.label: L-03
classifiedFindings.title: initiateMigration writes state after the external strategy.withdraw call (reentrancy ordering; Aderyn HIGH / Slither Medium) — guard- and trust-mitigated

classification.assetImpact: None demonstrated. initiateMigration realizes the strategy (external strategy.withdraw at L387) before writing migrationInfo at L408, but the function is nonReentrant and onlyMigrator, and the only callees are protocol-trusted (owner-configured IYieldStrategy and the phUSD minter), not attacker-controlled.
attackPath: 1. Static tools flag the write-after-call ordering on the terminal-migration entry point.
2. No reentrant path exists: nonReentrant blocks re-entry and the callee is trusted.
3. No exploit demonstrated.
classification.likelihood: negligible - requires a malicious/compromised IYieldStrategy, which is owner-trusted; nonReentrant blocks reentry regardless.
classification.assumptions: IYieldStrategy and phUSD are protocol-trusted (per project model).
classification.externalRequirements: Would require an attacker-controlled strategy callee (excluded by trust model).

classifiedFindings.justification: Informational. This is the automated-tool category C4 would normally invalidate (no demonstrated HM path; nonReentrant + trusted callee). It is NOT suppressed — it was deliberately preserved for the classifier to formally dispose in a visible channel (Law 1), rather than dropped by the sanitizer. Disposed to Informational with CEI-ordering hygiene guidance (move the L408 state write before the external call). No PoC required; QA bundle as the lowest-priority item.
